1.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties on these petitions filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
2. The prayers in both petitions are similar.

For convenience, we quote prayers as made in Writ Petition No.7595 of 2021which read thus:
Sopan Baburao Gore Decd. Thr. Lhr ... vs The National Highway Authority Of India ... on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194646592/
1 8 August 2024 Kiran Kawre 901-WP-7595-2021.DOC "a)This Hon'ble Court be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ or order,
direction and direct the Respondent Authority to carry out the physical survey of the land owned by the Petitioner as per the records and thereafter acquired the said land for purpose of widening of the Pune Nashik National Highway (NH50) (Pune Khed Section) of required, and pay the compensation to the Petitioners under the provisions Right to fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, by following due process of law.
b) Pending the hearing and final disposal of the present Writ Petition, the Respondent No.1 should not take direct possession of the land owned by the Petitioners for widening of the Pune - Nashik National Highway (NH-50) (Pune Khed Section);
c) Interim and ad-interim in terms of prayer clause (b) be granted.
d) Such other and further relief's be granted as the nature and circumstances of the case may be require."
3. The substantive prayer being (a) is made with an apprehension that the petitioners' land is required for the purpose of widening of the National Highway (NH - 50) at the hands of the National Highway Authority of India / Respondent No.1.

entities.text: Sopan Baburao Gore Decd. Thr. Lhr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The proceedings appear to have some history before this Court as there are several orders which are passed, suffice it to observe that NHAI has taken a consistent stand that the petitioners' land has not been acquired and there is no land acquisition award in acquiring the petitioners land.
Similar is the position taken by the State Government.
The State Government has also not placed on record any land acquisition award in relation to any prior widening of the NH - 50.
8 August 2024 Kiran Kawre 901-WP-7595-2021.DOC 4.
In this view of the matter, in our opinion, the prayers as made in the petition would not require adjudication.

In the event, the land is required by any of the authorities including by respondent No.1, in that event, the authority would be required to follow an appropriate procedure as known to law so as to acquire the petitioners' land and only till an award is passed and / or the necessary procedure as known to law under the National Highways Act, 1956 is followed, the petitioner cannot be dispossessed.
So is also the assurance of respondent No.1 that if at all the possession of the petitioners land is to be taken, it would be taken by following due procedure of law.

We accept such statement as made on behalf of respondent No.1.
5.
In the light of the above observations, further adjudication of the petition is not called for.
It is accordingly disposed of.
6. No costs.
(SOMASEKHAR SUNDARESAN, J.) (G. S. KULKARNI , J.) 8 August 2024 Kiran Kawre Sopan Baburao Gore Decd.
